key_insight: LabSafety Bench provides a standardized evaluation showing that large language models vary widely in their ability to identify laboratory hazards and assess risk, revealing important gaps in accuracy, calibration, and contextual understanding for safety‑critical lab tasks.
problem_solved: Fills the absence of a focused benchmark to measure how well LLMs recognize hazards and estimate laboratory risks, enabling systematic assessment before deploying models in safety‑sensitive scientific settings.
method: Assembled LabSafety Bench: curated scenarios and annotated hazards covering common lab environments, equipment, chemicals, and procedural risks.
Evaluated multiple LLMs on tasks including hazard identification, risk severity scoring, and recommended mitigations under varying contextual prompts.
Measured performance with quantitative metrics (accuracy, calibration, robustness to prompt/context changes) and categorized common failure modes.
impact: Helps AI/ML practitioners and lab stakeholders quantify where models are reliable or brittle for safety applications, informing model selection, mitigation strategies, and the need for human‑in‑the‑loop safeguards prior to real‑world deployment.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of LabSafety Bench: dataset → tasks (identify, score, mitigate) → evaluation metrics
Bar chart comparing model performance across tasks (identification, scoring, mitigation) with confidence intervals
Error/heatmap showing common failure modes by hazard category (chemical, equipment, procedural, biological)
Icon set: hazard symbols annotated with model confidence bands to visualize calibration and uncertainty
paper_title: Benchmarking large language models on safety risks in scientific laboratories
paper_authors: Yujun Zhou, Jingdong Yang, Yue Huang, Kehan Guo, Zoe Emory
